steps.title: Gather required materials
steps.instruction: Collect all reagents, consumables and media listed below with their catalog numbers: pipette tips (Mettler Toledo 17005872, 17005874, 17007089), 96‑well plate (VWR 82006‑636), 0.2 µm filter (Fisher 09‑719C), Petri plates (VWR 25384‑342), yeast strain BY4741, MoClo Yeast Toolkit (Addgene kit 1000000061; plasmids pYTK050, pYTK003, pYTK072, pYTK083, pYTK036, pYTK008, pYTK047, pYTK073, pYTK074, pYTK081, pYTK084), PCR template (cDNA, plasmid clone, etc.), NEB 5‑alpha Competent E. coli (C2987), DNA stain (Thermo Fisher S33102), T7 ligase (NEB M0318S), T4 ligase buffer (NEB B0202S), restriction enzymes BsaI (NEB R0535S) and BsmBI (NEB R0580S), LB plates with antibiotics (ampicillin 10835242001, spectinomycin PHR1426, chloramphenicol C0378), high‑fidelity polymerase KAPA HiFi (KK2601), Zymo DNA Clean&Concentrator‑25 kit (D4005), Zymo EZ Yeast Transformation II kit (T2001), optional 100 mM lithium acetate (Sigma L6883), Accuprime Pfx (Thermo 12344024), optional 5‑fluoroorotic acid (F5013), D‑sorbitol (S3889), Zymolyase (MP 320921), LB broth Lennox (BD 240210), YPD powder (BD 242820), agarose (Thermo 16500500), agar (SERVA 11396), yeast nitrogen base (BD 291940), ammonium sulfate (Sigma A4418), dextrose (Avantor 1919), SC‑Ura dropout powder (Sigma Y1501). Also prepare the media and solutions described in the Recipes section.

steps.title: Design guide RNAs
steps.instruction: Using Geneious, E‑CRISP or similar, design at least two 20‑bp gRNA sequences targeting the open reading frame of the yeast gene to be replaced. Ensure the target site will be absent after replacement (e.g., for HEM2 use sg1 = GGATTATCGGAGATGAATAG on the non‑coding strand and sg2 = CCTGGTACCAAGGATCCAGT on the coding strand). Design multiple gRNAs in parallel to hedge against low activity.

steps.title: Order and prepare oligos
steps.instruction: Order forward and reverse oligonucleotides for each gRNA with Golden‑Gate compatible overhangs: forward = 5'‑GACTTT + 20‑bp guide (e.g., GACTTTGGATTATCGGAGATGAATAG for sg1); reverse = 5'‑AAAC + reverse‑complement of guide + AA (e.g., AAACCTATTCATCTCCGATAATCCAA for sg1). Order at 50 µM concentration.

steps.title: Anneal oligonucleotides
steps.instruction: For each gRNA, mix 20 µl total containing 50 µM forward and 50 µM reverse oligo (final 50 µM each). Run thermocycler: 95 °C 5 min, 55 °C 15 min, 25 °C 15 min. No phosphorylation is needed.

steps.title: First Golden Gate into shuttle vector
steps.instruction: Set up a 10 µl Golden Gate reaction (insert: pYTK050) with the following: 40 fmol annealed dsOligo, 20 fmol pYTK050, 1.0 µl 10× NEB T4 buffer (B0202S), 0.5 µl NEB T7 ligase (M0318S), 0.5 µl NEB BsmBI (R0580S), add ddH₂O to 10 µl. Incubate according to standard Golden Gate protocol. Transform 5‑α NEB competent E. coli (C2987), plate on LB agar with chloramphenicol 170 µg/ml. After overnight growth, view colonies under UV; pick white (non‑GFP) colonies, grow in liquid culture and miniprep plasmid. Optional: sequence plasmid to verify gRNA insert.

steps.title: Second Golden Gate to assemble gRNA cassette
steps.instruction: Prepare a 10 µl reaction containing: 20 fmol gRNA‑on‑pYTK050 (from step 5), 20 fmol ConL1 (pYTK003), 20 fmol ConRE (pYTK072), 20 fmol AmpR‑ColE1 (pYTK083), 1.0 µl 10× NEB T4 buffer, 0.5 µl NEB T7 ligase, 0.5 µl NEB BsaI (R0535S), water to 10 µl. Perform Golden Gate, transform into NEB 5‑α cells, plate on LB agar with ampicillin 60 µg/ml. Pick white colonies, grow and purify plasmid.

steps.title: Third Golden Gate to create CRISPR plasmid
steps.instruction: Assemble a 10 µl reaction with: 20 fmol gRNA cassette plasmid (from step 6), 20 fmol Cen6‑Ura cassette* (assembled from YTK plasmids 008, 047, 073, 074, 081, 084), 20 fmol Cas9 plasmid pYTK036, 1.0 µl 10× NEB T4 buffer, 0.5 µl NEB T7 ligase, 0.5 µl NEB BsmBI, water to 10 µl. Transform into NEB 5‑α cells, plate on LB agar with kanamycin 50 µg/ml. Pick white colonies, grow, and miniprep. Quantify plasmid and dilute to a standardized concentration; use 500 ng per yeast transformation.

steps.title: Design repair‑template DNA
steps.instruction: Obtain the genomic sequence of the target yeast gene (old gene) and the coding sequence (CDS) of the replacement gene (new gene) without introns. Keep the native yeast stop codon intact. Using Geneious or similar, edit the old‑gene sequence to insert the new CDS at the desired locus. Design PCR primers that anneal ~25 bp to the 5′ and 3′ ends of the new CDS and also to the adjacent 5′ and 3′ UTRs, providing homology arms of at least 70 bp (up to 170 bp if needed). Primer length will be ~90 bp total.

steps.title: Amplify repair template
steps.instruction: Perform high‑fidelity PCR (e.g., KAPA HiFi, KK2601) using the primers from step 7. Run test reactions with several polymerases if needed. Aim for ≥5 µg template DNA from a 50 µl reaction (10 µg optional for difficult loci). Verify product size by agarose gel electrophoresis; non‑specific bands are acceptable as long as the correct band is present. Purify PCR product with Zymo DNA Clean&Concentrator‑25 kit (D4005), elute in 25 µl double‑distilled water to obtain ~400–800 ng/µl DNA.

steps.title: Prepare competent yeast cells
steps.instruction: Use the Zymo EZ Yeast Transformation II kit (T2001) following the manufacturer’s protocol. The EZ 1 solution may be replaced with 100 mM lithium acetate (Sigma L6883) without loss of efficiency. Grow 2 ml BY4741 culture, process to yield 100 µl competent cells (sufficient for two 50 µl transformations).

steps.title: Perform yeast transformation
steps.instruction: For each transformation, combine in a tube: 50 µl competent yeast, 500 µl EZ 3 solution (or equivalent), 500 ng CRISPR plasmid (from step 6), 5 µg repair‑template DNA (up to 50 µl total volume). Incubate at 30 °C as instructed by the kit, then plate on SD‑Ura (uracil dropout) agar plates. For a control, repeat the reaction without repair DNA to assess gRNA cleavage efficiency.

steps.title: Incubate transformed plates
steps.instruction: Incubate plates at 30 °C. Colonies typically appear after 1–3 days; if the replacement imposes a fitness defect, allow up to 6 days.

steps.title: Pick colonies for screening
steps.instruction: Select up to 12 colonies per transformation, transfer each into 50 µl sterile water using a pipette tip. Store suspensions at 4 °C; they remain usable for up to 2 weeks. (Optional: use a 12‑channel pipette to process all colonies simultaneously.)

steps.title: Prepare lysates for colony PCR
steps.instruction: For each colony suspension, add 15 µl zymolyase solution (see Recipes). Incubate 30 min at room temperature, then 15 min at 37 °C, then 5 min at 95 °C to inactivate enzymes.

steps.title: Colony PCR to confirm integration
steps.instruction: Set up 20 µl PCR reactions using Accuprime Pfx (Thermo 12344024): 1 µl lysate as template, confirmation primer pair that spans the 5′ junction (forward anneals to yeast UTR, reverse anneals within the new gene). Also set up a positive‑control PCR with primers targeting the ERG13 promoter (forward CGAACTGGATGAGATGGCCG, reverse CATGCTGCACCTTTTATAGTAATTTGGC) to verify lysate quality. Run reactions, then analyze products on an agarose gel. A ~300 bp band with the confirmation primers indicates correct integration.

steps.title: Propagate confirmed clones
steps.instruction: Inoculate fresh YPD liquid culture with the original water suspension of each colony that gave the correct PCR band. Grow to desired density for downstream work.

steps.title: Cure CRISPR plasmid
steps.instruction: Streak confirmed clones on YPD agar. From each streak, pick 10 individual colonies and patch each onto parallel YPD and SD‑Ura plates. Incubate at 30 °C for 3 days (extend to 6 days if growth is slow). Colonies that grow on YPD but not on SD‑Ura have lost the CRISPR plasmid. (Optional: counter‑select on 5‑fluoroorotic acid plates (FOA, Sigma F5013) to force loss of URA3, but note that FOA can select for URA3 mutations rather than true plasmid loss.)

steps.title: Prepare media and solutions (Recipes)
steps.instruction:
Prepare the following reagents as described:
- Zymolyase solution (50 ml): dissolve 9.11 g D‑sorbitol (Sigma S3889) in 50 ml distilled water to make 1 M sorbitol, autoclave, add 0.25 g zymolyase (MP 320921), aliquot, store at –20 °C.
- Lithium acetate 100 mM (40 ml): dissolve 0.408 g lithium acetate dihydrate (Sigma L6883) in 40 ml distilled water, filter‑sterilize (0.2 µm), store at room temperature.
- LB medium (1 L): weigh 25 g LB powder (BD 240210); for solid plates add 15 g agar (SERVA 11396). Dissolve in 1 L water, autoclave, cool to 60–70 °C, pour into Petri dishes, solidify, store at 4 °C.
- YPD medium (1 L): weigh 50 g YPD powder (BD 242820); for plates add 20 g agar. Dissolve, autoclave, cool, pour, solidify, store at 4 °C.
- SD‑Ura medium (1 L): weigh 1.5 g yeast nitrogen base without amino acids (BD 291940), 5 g ammonium sulfate (Sigma A4418), 20 g dextrose (Avantor 1919), 2 g SC‑Ura dropout powder (Sigma Y1501); for plates add 20 g agar. Dissolve, autoclave, cool, pour, solidify, store at 4 °C.
